Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
To say that I'm disappointed would be a gross understatement.

To clarify, The Legend of Zelda is my favourite series in gaming and has never failed to impress, move and floor me with every one of the games.

This is the very first time I've felt let down. And it hurts. I so desperately want to agree with all of the rave reviews, but I just can't.

To me, Tears of the Kingdom is effectively a repurposed Breath of the Wild.

- There are no fundamental differences with the way this game looks plays or feels. The combat mechanics are untouched and play exactly as they did in BotW (flurry rush and bullet time galore). The fusion mechanic makes the weapons look cooler and adds more longevity to even the weakest of base weapons... but I struggle to care beyond aesthetics when the combat encounters are the exact same mechanically against opponents that are also largely the exact same ones from BotW.

- The new mechanics are fun to muck around with, particularly "Ascend", however the whole "Ultrahand" vehicle building gimmick never really stuck for me. I only ever engaged with it as a matter of convenience in the overworld, and while the shrine puzzles were mostly well designed, it all felt a bit samey after a while. I understand that this is preference, but when this is the foundation of new mechanics that the game is built around in the stead of actual puzzles akin to the classic titles that made them as fun as they are... I don't see it as a worthy successor.

- The dungeons themselves are an improvement over the Divine Beasts - however still follow that same formula of do the thing five times then fight the boss. Also, here are the five places you need to go to marked on your map from the get go. It's all so watered down. Half the fun of the old dungeons was navigating, now that's all done for you! At least we've got actual bosses now good god, the Ganon Blights were dismal in BotW.

- The story is bad. It's a bad story. Not necessarily because of the content, but certainly because of the structure and how it's conveyed to the player. There is absolutely no agency whatsoever as soon as the intro to the game is over. They just do the memory thing again, except this time they aren't even Link's memories and he therefore has no role in the story whatsoever. It's a story that has already happened that the main character isn't involved in that barely affects the game's actual proceedings??? How are we supposed to care? It's so clear that NIntendo didn't want to sacrifice the freedom and wanted to have it both ways, which has resulted in one of the most poorly delivered stories I've ever seen with no weight whatsoever. This is helped in no part thanks to Link's complete lack of characterisation. He is as stiff as he ever was in BotW but at least in the game it was somewhat justifiable as he was a soldier with amnesia. They even had an in game explanation for it. You'd think after years of peace with Zelda he'd have dropped the act just a little. It makes it so embarrassing when scenes are supposed to have weight and he's just standing there looking like he's fresh out of a lobotomy procedure. Agonising to watch. I know he's always been somewhat of a blank slate but come on!

- Ganondorf, as a result, is a total wasted opportunity. He is hardly in the game at all. Could they not have sacrificed just a smidge of the freedom to provide a sense of stakes, weight and agency to this game?! We already got boundless freedom in BotW, reign it in a bit!

- The sky and depths definitely exist. They both harbour some great main story stuff, but the remainder of both is just lacklustre. Sky has a load of islands to discover but they all amount to the same thing of just super simple shrine puzzles and then a Rauru's Blessing. The dephs are even worse. A great big giant pit of the same biome strecthed across the enitre map with a whole ton of copy paste enemies and armour from the amiibos. On that note, there is barely any new armour, which is hugely dissapoiting.

- I don't know some of the new bosses are cool, but there aren't nearly enough. The caves on the surface are cool for a while but most look and play the same. There are barely any new enemy types, hardly matters though because the mechanics are the exact same and aren't conducive to engaging combat. The Map is the same, they've revamped it with different enemy base layouts and way more of them but who cares when it's just the same assets from BotW but more abundant?

I'm being harsh I know. This isn't a bad game, just one that's disappointed me greatly especially considering the development time. I have had enough of this formula, this franchise needs at least some amount of linearity to work!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Yo seriously y'all, the building the cool little contraptions is fun but they're selling us BoTW with a new coat of paint here. Everything that's new like the caves and the sky Islands and even the depths get tedious maybe a few hours in after you realize these locations follow the exact same formula every time you dive in.

Caves and wells have a stalnox or another boss enemy in them, sometimes a shrine, and a Bubbul gem. Exact same setup every time.

In the sky Islands, you either fight a Zonai guy, go get a crystal or do a jumping challenge. There's no sky cities, there's nothing really happening up there.

The depths are the funnest to explore, until you realize there's not much down there. You're only really going to end up down there if you're farming Poes and Zonaite.

With the exception of like 4 armor sets, EVERY ARMOR SET HAS BEEN RECYCLED FROM THE FIRST GAME. Even the ugly ass Gordon armor. This was ultimately what made me want to drop the game before I finished it. Even Dark Souls reuses some of it's maps, but at least they throw us a bone and give us new equipment to get excited about.

The weapons all look like **** now. You found a cool sword? Too bad it's tarnished and you're gonna have to fuse it with a **** huge boko bat to do anything with it anyway.

And yeah, the weapons still break. The story is pretty braindead, I won't spoil it but it follows a pretty similar formula.

There is no new game plus, you beat Ganon and you're back to your last save.

There's only one new settlement to visit, no new towns or cities to explore. They slapped some environment changes into some of the existing towns to make them seem "fresh" but there's really no new services or interesting NPCs in any of them.

Horses function almost exactly the same. Same equipment, same customization. You can buff their skills, which is nice, but that's it. You still can't register any of the wacky mount types like Satori, the Skeletal Horses or the deer at the stable.

They removed the Amiibo functionality from the Wolf-Link Amiibo for seemingly no reason. I suppose you can get the sages to fill a similar role but I don't get why that was removed.

You're going to be spending most of your time in the menus fusing stuff while fighting enemies, which can get tedious fast. The dungeons are a bit bit more creative than the Divine Beasts, but not by much.

If you were a big fan of the master cycle, that's gone now. You could technically build a motorbike with the ultrahand ability but it'll look like crap in comparison.

The Zonai shrines are asset flips of the original Sheikah shrines, and just as boring and tedious. They don't even explain where the Sheikah **** went.

Koroks haven't changed much, some of them are a little bit more creative and employ you to use your contraptions, but at the end of the day it's just filler.

All of the music and sound effects are exactly the same from the first game. They have added some new sound effects for the Zonai stuff.

The Zonai stuff has an arbitrary distance counter before the components poof out of existence, doesn't matter how much upgrading you do 400 hours in, no fun allowed with papa Nintendo

The into sequence layout exactly follows that of the first game (Ghost man guides you through the tutorial and then disappears)

Enemy variety is still lacking. You have Lynels, Talus, Hinox, etc. There's a few new enemies but they generally have been created to fill out the new locations (caves, sky Islands, the depths, etc)

The only pros I can count are:
- It runs quite a bit better than BoTW
- All Amiibo items are now found organically in game (but again, copy pasted assets)
- You don't have to drop **** before opening a chest now if you want to swap the contents with something you already have

Anyway I can go on, but man, after playing ToTK to completion the only thing that I'm left thinking is "what the **** has Nintendo been doing the past 6 years"? The sound design team hasn't done **** the animators and modelers have had to make minimal changes to everything short of reskinning a couple of assets, literally 90% of the map is unchanged. The whole game feels like a mod. What in the fresh hell took so long to pump this out? Seriously, this must be the ultimate attempt to try and justify to their shareholders that they can re-make a game with a reduced development crew and still make a fortune off it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
One of the greats. The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom is an excellent sequel to Breath of the Wild, Improving upon almost everything in the game. The shrines are much more diverse. The map has been expanded on massively providing beautiful scenery up in the sky islands while providing a sense of mystery and exploration in the hostile world of the depths.
While this game is a masterpiece in its own right, I feel it struggles with its place in the Legend of Zelda franchise. I say this because (due to a specific storyline) there is so much retconning in the game that it becomes almost jarring. Not only that but I felt that the Ganon fight was poorly set up with the teasing of a showdown only to make you run around solving dull puzzles before you can reach him again.

One of ToTK's biggest flaws in my opinion is that, while sharing almost the same surface map with BoTW, ToTK had a lot less boots in the ground moments. There were no real challenges in terrain or combat, any issue could just be solved with a rocket or hoverbike and that personally removed any of the moment-to-moment fun for me.

While I understand that many players enjoyed ToTK, I found many sections of the game far too tedious and dull. The dungeons were far too formulaic and drawn out. I found myself so frustrated with the mundanity of so many of these dungeons that I just cheesed the game with rockets and recall just so I could get it over with.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Having never experienced the original Breath of the Wild, I approached Tears of the Kingdom with fresh eyes. The initial stages of the game were enjoyable, leading me to complete three Regional Phenomena quests and explore a considerable portion of the Depths. Yet, over time, my experience was marred by a growing sense of irritation.

My most significant issue lies with the controls. Nintendo appears to be attempting to squeeze too much functionality into a single console controller. This results in a game experience where players find themselves spending an excessive amount of their playtime navigating through menus. Constant interruptions to select a new weapon, shield, or bow, or to consume food, become a prominent part of the game. For those seeking a more laid-back gaming session, this could become a source of annoyance due to the incessant need to switch to a menu to choose an option. The interruptions are relentless.

When it comes to world design and the sheer variety of activities, the game scores a perfect '10'. While it's true that the graphics are bound by the system's limitations, they remain quite admirable. Though they occasionally appear pixelated, they are still beautiful within their constraints. No one expects PlayStation 5 level graphics, but what's presented here is not just acceptable, but artistically, very commendable.

In conclusion, I rate the game a 7. While it offers a fantastic world to explore, the overall experience is significantly hindered by an overly complex and tedious control scheme.

Biggest complaints, barren sky and underground, overall game play is easy, cooking and clothing become fairly useless as most of it doesnt do anything that is actually needed to complete the game, and worst of all the very short and low difficulty in the dungeons. I would go for a smaller world that has more content, or missions that give meaningful rewards or add to the "must do's" to move forward or access other new content . So the game gets a 7 because it's not fair to score too low because it is well-made, but definitely not a 10 because it is not far off from breath of the wild.

Bon, le constat est très amer pour ce Zelda, c'est très décevant de voir qu'une licence aussi novatrice que l'ai normalement Zelda ne l'ai plus depuis ce nouvel opus, en effet à première vue il semble que le jeu est changé du tout au tout mais ce n'est qu'illusion.

- Scénario au fraise.

- Map identique à la précédente.

- Qualité graphique plus que déplorable malgré les énormes effort que ce jeu demande à la Switch. - Recyclage d'une grande partie de la bande sonore original.

- Personnage trop amical malgré que cet univers est censé être en total perdition et que cet univers devrait dévoiler le côté obscur de cet deuxième partie.


La nouvelle mécanique de gameplay est très bien mise en place dès les premières heures de jeu, c'est un réel plaisir de remanier le jeu avec toutes les nouveautés, cependant après quelques heures on ne réfléchit plus autant qu'au début de cet belle aventure.

Je suis très déçu que ce jeu à était sur noter par certains média le dévoilant comme une innovation importante par rapport au précédent opus, alors que tous cela aurait très bien pu être un DLC du précédent volume, ce qui me désole profondément.

En outre je recommande vivement ce jeu au personne n'ayant pas fait breath of the Wild avant ou l'ayant fait depuis X années.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
If you played BotW, don’t get this game because you’ve already played it. This game has its origins as BotW DLC and it shows - it’s messed right up that they charge a whopping $70 for 4 extra gigs of poor game design. If you didn’t play BotW, you’re clear.

While I’m not going to pretend that I didn’t have a good time with this game, I’m also not going to pretend I didn’t have a good time because it was Breath of the Wild again. The two heavily and maliciously advertised regions in the game are either complete gimmicks or just straight up boring and a slog to get through. The dungeons are on average much better than the Divine Beasts except for the water dungeon because of the cognitive dissonance of it being in the sky and the last dungeon in the game (not the final area) is straight up just a tech demo. The story is just a slightly altered repeat of its predecessor with a whole new cast you’re never going to meet. The gameplay is “better” especially since it fixes the main issue with weapons that people had in the last game. The game however shamelessly lies to you in order to make ends meet. No like seriously. In the numbers and the world itself. I have a whole 13.3 MB documents of me going on a rant about this game I can share if requested.

I’m saying this as a diehard fan of this franchise and it infuriates me that this is what we got. Can’t in good faith recommend this to any Zelda veteran. If it was in the $30 -$40 price range this game would be an well deserved 9-10 /10 but if you’re going to list yourself as a higher than average AAA game at $70 you better have the bite to back up that bark and this game just doesn’t have that.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
In only 1 word: DISSAPOINTED. But not only with this title but with previous Breath of The Wild too. Why I say that? Well, I'm essentially referring to the direction in which the franchise has evolved.

I consider myself a huge fan of The Legend of Zelda, in fact my personal top 5 games of all history includes Ocarina and Majora's.
In my opinion the following games of the saga were only a bit step behind those ones, but we are talking about truly masterpieces too. I refer to Twilight Princess, Wind Waker, Skyward Sword and Link's Awakening.

It seems the company has forgotten that one of the hallmarks of the saga is the innovation. Every game launched since Ocarina of Time is very very different from the previous one. The originality and uniqueness present on each release is over. This TOTK is just a copy-paste of BOTW with very little mods and it's very sad.

In the first 3 hr of playing this TOTK, I only talked with 8-9 stupid automatas and a spirit (not counting the intro when Zelda talks to you). The rest was boring and basic exploration, 2 tiny dungeons and 5 min combat. In my opinion the evolution taken by the company on this saga is clearly wrong.

This huge world is too much for Link, most part is empty and the gameplay is mainly based on exploration, gathering, cooking, climbing, walking and repeat and then repeat again. Don't expect here to see an Elden Ring universe full of life with very different and captivating scenarios but without forget including those great "closed" areas of previous Soul's games. Because one of the funniest and challenging parts of an adventure game like this one was supposed to the challenge of complete the great dungeons/temples that now are a mere shadow of those ones. In adittion final bosses are way too easy and derivative.

The landscapes now are all very similar within itselves and the gameplay is boring. Why they left behind all the charming stories that was a key element of the game? Because don't forget that The Legend of Zelda is a game about stories, relationships with people and all vested with an awesome halo of fantasy and magic with hints of epic and sometimes tragic. Now all these elements gone and it doesn't seem to come back soon (at least while people continue loving the path they have taken with last 2 games...)

Even the epic music that featured most of the Zelda videogames and made us to fall in love with it (how to forget saria's song, bolero of fire, gerudo valley, ballad of the goddess, kakariko village, romani ranch...) has now turned into boring and typical tunes without soul.

Definitely I can't recommend anyone to play this game.

Review:
The Legend of Zelda is my favorite game series. I played all games since Ocarina of Time and enjoyed all of them. This game is unbelievably big with a crazy amount of things to see and do, but that is also the reason i dont give it a higher score. Everything feels so overwhelming, and was very confused on why i had to do a lot of seemingly unrelated side quests in order to progress in the main story. I feel like they are called side quests for a reason, they shouldnt be mandatory to finish a game.
For example: After i got beat by Ganon in my first fight with him i come to realize is was missing a sage (Mineru). Now i need to do a quests that you can find in Kakariko village in order to progress, if you dont get the hint like i did you will search the map for mutiple hours before you know you had to go to kakariko village and do this quest. Now after you do try doing this quests you need to do a lot of side quests in order to get some purah tablet functions (scanner+) so you can find the electric clothing pieces. After hours of tedious boring quests you can finally find the sixth sage and you are ready to fight Ganon.. But in order to know where Ganon is, you got to, you guessed it, do more side missions with the researcher girl in the lookout posts. These are some of the most boring missions ever, where you follow statues for hours in the underground, while you just want to finish the game and kill Ganon. After all these hours of doing boring side quests, you come to realize Ganon was just under hyrule castly.. Why all the sidetracking just to get this information?

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
TL;DR It's good. Most likely you won't regret playing it, especially if you haven't played Breath of the wild yet. The critic is exaggerating it (it wouldn't deserve a 10), but it's definitely a high quality video game with a lot of care put into it.
On the "full price DLC" debate: it does, in fact, feel like DLC, but there is so much content that it's well worth its price. In fact, most DLC would be overpriced compared to this game.
However, I wouldn't recommend buying a Nintendo Switch exclusively for Tears of the Kingdom, or any single videogame, really.

PROS
-Some of the best environmental puzzle solving around which encourages yout creativity and rewards unintended solutions
-A highly-acclaimed physics system that manages to surprise you after years of playing
-A LOT of content (and it's mostly good)
-It's really cinematic at times (especially the music, the dungeons, the bosses and the skydiving sections)

CONS
-The story is weak and incoherent
-Outdated graphics and performance dips in some situations (the day one patch helps, install it)

YOU DECIDE
-Not only the main map, but all the formulas (shrines, memories, 4 main dungeons) from the previous game are brought over
-There is a lot of building to be done and it can get goofy

I understand that it’s a similar formula to BOTW, and if people didn’t click with the 2017 title, they believe they might not click with this one. Still, for me, those individuals should try TOTK because it combines the formula for BOTW but brings back elements from classic Zeldas they have wished for. This game isn’t anything less than a 10. I get we all have different tastes, but having different tastes does not warrant giving an masterfully crafted game a low score. Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
My expectations for this game were huge and it delivered.

The gameplay feels like a natural and improved evolution of Breath of the Wild's. The combat is AMAZING, with the Fuse mechanic making it more engaging and challenging. The world is so big I feel I have tons of hours of exploration ahead of me. And the story, so far, feels more present than that of BOTW's.

Also, it has lots of QoL improvements, like the new menus or (thanks, thanks, thanks) the ability to discard a weapon when your slots are full and you open a chest that contains another weapon. I'm still a little speechless after 2 days of playing this game non stop. Here's to many more days of fun to come!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I'm a huge Zelda fan. I've already played for over 60 hours, and WHAT A GAME! I've completed 67% of the shrines, collected over 100 Korok seeds, explored 90% of the map, and completed half of the dungeons. It will probably take me another 60 hours to finish all the shrines and complete the game.

Pros (in comparison to Breath of the Wild):
*The gameplay is more enjoyable.
*The map is significantly larger.
*The cinematics are amazing and have improved a lot.
*The dungeons feel almost like proper dungeons again.
*There is a greater variety of shrines.
*New map bosses and a plethora of new weapon possibilities through fusing.
*Overall, I estimate it to be 20% better than BotW.

Cons (related to the Zelda genre):
*While the game boasts impressive art and visuals, its appearance is becoming outdated and falls short in comparison to BotW's market at launch.
*The dungeons are still short and easy.
*The dungeon bosses are easy and lack clever design.
*There are practically no moments of hard thinking or struggle.
*The depths feel somewhat repetitive, and their design is not very appealing.
*I miss some of the old items, particularly a musical instrument and hook shot.
*Many Zelda fans are concerned that Nintendo might completely abandon the old genre, especially 2D. But please, Nintendo, don't do that! Keep both styles! A Link Between Worlds was amazing!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This is the most creative adventure game I've ever played. The depth of the gameplay and the feeling of accomplishment when you figure something out in your own custom way is unmatched. It truly makes you feel like you invented the solution to the puzzles yourself.

The powers are better than BotW and each challenge you encounter perfectly forces you to learn how to use them on your own. There are more kinds of things to explore like caves and wells. There are some familiar items and enemies but also many new ones, especially in the sky and deep underground. The map is NOT the same! There are three maps! One for ground, one for sky, and one for deep underground where it's completely dark and all connected. The sky puzzles are amazing! The ground map has the same regions as BotW but they are different this time around. And the deep underground is done very well with the light sources that you can use to light the darkness.

Many things have been upgraded and improved or expanded upon. I haven't had this much fun playing a game in... I don't know, because this game is such a unique feeling of creativity mixed with Nintendo's highest quality design, its like I'm playing the first of a new genre. I think this is my first metacritic review. I just had to stand up for how amazing this game really is. It kind of like Legos and everybody loves Legos. Don't listen to these miserable people, this game is a must play. Relax and have fun. A new kind of great open world game is here. :)

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Zelda Tears of the Kingdom est pour moi la concrétisation de la formule Breath of the wild. Tout ce qu'il propose en gameplay est bien meilleur que son prédécesseur.
Nous pouvions contrôler le métal, maintenant nous pouvons contrôler tout type de matières et les assembler entre elles.
Nous pouvions arrêter le temps sur une cible, maintenant nous la faisons remonter le temps.
L'escalade vous fatigue, ou il pleut un peu trop souvent ? Infiltration règlera vos problèmes.
Je ne vais pas vous expliciter toutes les améliorations de ce jeu vis à vis de BOTW tellement il y en a.

Alors oui la technique n'est pas au niveau des PS5 et j'en passe, mais ce n'est pas l'objectif d'une switch. D'ailleurs la direction artistique du jeu permet de s'évader dans un univers enchanteur et clairement immersif.
Je peux aussi entendre que le faite de construire certains véhicules peu déranger, mais hormis quelques phases de jeu, ce n'est absolument pas obligatoire, et les moyens de déplacement de BOTW sont toujours d'actualités (paravoile, cheval, téléportation,...).

TOTK n'est aucunement un DLC mais l'aboutissement d'une formule qui ferait presque passer BOTW pour un brouillon. Et je conseille à tout ceux qui n'ont pas fait le jeu de s'y mettre, vous vous perdrez dans un monde aussi riche que vaste et vous ne verrez pas le temps passé.
Si BOTW était une ode à l'aventure sans limite, TOTK est une ode à la liberté et à l'imagination.

Its weakest point is the construction system: creative at first, but ultimately over-used and sometimes disruptive to the game’s flow. Even so, TOTK delivers a  memorable adventure for most players.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
I think my score gets extra points because i didn't play botw. For me, the exploration was a new thing in Zelda games, i don't know if it felt the same for players who played both totk and botw. Overall this game is awesome, but has a few major let downs. 
 
The dungeons are really boring compared to older Zelda titles. In totk all dungeons are based on one idea, go to four or five different places and then fight the boss. At least the last dungeon has more character.
 
Also the story doesn't go anywhere while you complete the main four dungeons around Hyrule. After each dungeon you get almost exactly the same cut scene every time, about the imprisoning war. It is one of the most boring ways for a game to tell a story.

This review turned out to be way more negative then i wanted. I still love the game. The ending is really epic and overall i think the game was best after the four temples.

The gameplay and exploration is really fun, sometimes i played the game for like 5 hours without noticing. The abilities were really fun and creative. My favourite has to be ascend. It makes coming out from caves so much easier. The Zonai devices was a really cool addition as well. Building vehicles was fun and a really easy way of exploring the depths.

My score still remains a 9 even though the game has it's flaws. It might not be my favourite Zelda game, but it still was an epic and fun journey!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Breath of the Wild was my favorite game of all time, and this game just improved on it in every way. Better story, better options to move around the map, more stuff to do, this game has it all. The Fuse and Ultrahand abilities keep the game fresh, so every adventure or quest I go on feels unique. Plus the sheer amount of content in this game is insane. In BOTW there was quite a bit of empty space where there was just nothing going on. However, in TOTK, it feels like there’s always something going on wherever you go. The ground level itself feels so much more involved than in BOTW. There’s npcs all over the place to talk to and help out. The shrines seem a bit more sparing on the surface than in BOTW since they are split between the sky and the surface, but that’s made up for by everything else that there is on the surface. Ultrahand allows for some great quests and shrines that BOTW can’t even compare to. Your time will be well spent pretty much anywhere you go on the surface. And if you find yourself lost about what to do next, there’s always the sky islands and the depths. There’s literally always something to do in this game, and I don’t foresee myself 100%ing this game for months.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom is a game that deserves every accolade it receives, for it embodies the essence of limitless possibilities and introduces groundbreaking mechanics seldom seen in the realm of video games. This latest installment not only showcases remarkable innovation, but it flawlessly executes these novel features, defying expectations and proving itself bug-free throughout countless hours of gameplay.

One of the game's greatest strengths lies in its near-infinite potential for tackling its diverse challenges. The developers have masterfully crafted a world that encourages players to think creatively and adapt to various situations. The choices at our disposal are seemingly boundless, allowing us to approach each hurdle with an unparalleled level of freedom. The depth and breadth of these possibilities are awe-inspiring, leaving players with a sense of astonishment and a thirst for exploration.

Furthermore, the introduction of new mechanics is a testament to the game's innovative nature. These mechanics not only broaden the horizons of the Zelda franchise, but they also demonstrate a boldness rarely seen in video games. While other titles shy away from implementing such intricate actions due to the potential problems they may create, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom fearlessly embraces them. The result is a seamless integration of mechanics that open up thousands of possibilities, enriching the gameplay experience beyond imagination.

Remarkably, despite the complexity and ambition of the game, not a single bug mars the experience. The attention to detail and the dedication of the development team shine through, as they have meticulously crafted a polished and bug-free adventure. This level of quality is a testament to their commitment to delivering an exceptional gaming experience, and it ensures that players can immerse themselves fully in the world without any technical distractions.

While Tears of the Kingdom maintains the beloved aesthetic style of its predecessor, it is the captivating storyline that truly captivates players. Though it adheres to the classic Zelda formula, it manages to surpass expectations, delivering a narrative that not only meets but exceeds even the loftiest of expectations. It strikes the perfect balance between familiarity and innovation, captivating both newcomers and long-time fans alike. The story takes unexpected twists and turns, pulling at our heartstrings and evoking a range of emotions throughout the journey.

In conclusion, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom stands as a testament to the magic of adventure and the boundless potential of video games. Its almost infinite array of possibilities for approaching challenges, combined with groundbreaking mechanics flawlessly implemented, is nothing short of awe-inspiring. The absence of any bugs reinforces the dedication and craftsmanship behind this masterpiece.

Moreover, the game retains the iconic Zelda aesthetic while delivering a story that surpasses expectations, leaving players with a sense of wonder and fulfillment. Tears of the Kingdom is a true gem that enriches the Zelda legacy and sets new standards for the Zelda’s saga.

P.D. To those who have expressed their opinion about TLoZ: TotK as if it were just an overrated and generic DLC... Perhaps there has been a slight confusion regarding the expectations that were set.

Let us remember that Tears of the Kingdom is, in fact, a sequel. As such, it builds upon the rich history and gameplay that have characterized the Zelda franchise. We can't expect a sequel to completely reinvent the wheel, can we?

Now, let's discuss those who believe that the story is too short and that the rest of the content boils down to trivial add-ons. In the Zelda series, there has always been a special magic in exploring environments, unraveling secrets, and immersing oneself in side quests. After all, that's part of the fun! So, perhaps, a little more appreciation is needed for the intricate and holistic nature of the Zelda experience.

In summary, dear players, I invite you to embrace the essence and charm of Tears of the Kingdom. It is a sequel that builds upon its predecessors, providing a captivating and challenging adventure. So, before judging it as a mere DLC or undermining its content, take a moment to immerse yourself in the world of Hyrule and discover the wonders that await.

May your future adventures in Tears of the Kingdom be filled with awe and excitement!

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Ok, now I have finished this game and I can write a review.
The game was really good but I have to take some points off.

There was no postgame after ganondorf!
-This time I was definitely waiting for there to be postgame: some new side quests would have opened up and I could have explored the rest of the world and help rebuild whole Hyrule.

MAP
-Sky islands were fun and the underground world is huge!
-But I expected to find slightly different biomes there, tough I won't take any points off from this.
-Still.. With this game alone I wasn't quite able to fully achieve that same adventuring feeling than in Botw. Mostly because I already knew every major location on the ground, even tough there were a lot of caves and new enemies.
-I would have liked that they expanded the hyrule ground map even little and add new cities (even one) and would have made the old cities bigger!

RUNES
-All the runes were good/great and somewhat surprisingly I liked the Ascend
the most!

WEAPONS
-Weapons still break but fuse was ok/fun so no points off. Tough I still would prefer that you would be able to build/upgrade your own weapons with blacksmith/anvil and they wouldn't break

SHRINES & DUNGEONS
-the shrines were generally more fun than in Botw.
-I liked these dungeons better than Divine beasts

Summary
-I would say it is as good as botw but for new players it's even better.
But for those who already completed Botw and are really familiar with the old the map,
you might not be able to get the same level of adventure feeling when exploring on ground, witch is a HUGE part of the game.

But since this is direct sequel.. If you think Botw and Totk as one experience, then totk is pretty much a perfect postgame for Botw! ...well it's kinda overly large to be just postgame but if I think it this way then its 100/100!

Next game should be on whole new world! third time would be way too much..

Zelda is an iconic video game franchise that has been entertaining gamers for decades. With its rich storytelling, captivating gameplay, and memorable characters, it is no wonder that Zelda is beloved by so many.

One of the standout features of Zelda is its immersive world-building. From the sprawling fields of Hyrule to the treacherous dungeons and mysterious temples, every corner of the Zelda universe feels alive and full of adventure. Players are encouraged to explore every nook and cranny, uncovering secrets and discovering new challenges along the way.

But it's not just the world that makes Zelda so special. The series is also known for its memorable characters, from the heroic Link to the devious Ganon, and the various races and creatures that inhabit the world. Each character has their own unique personality and backstory, making them feel like real people rather than just game characters.

The gameplay in Zelda is also top-notch, with a perfect balance of action, puzzle-solving, and exploration. Players are challenged to use their wits and skills to overcome obstacles and defeat enemies, but the game never feels frustrating or unfair.

Overall, Zelda is a must-play for any gamer. With its timeless storytelling, unforgettable characters, and engaging gameplay, it is sure to provide hours of entertainment and leave a lasting impression on anyone who plays it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The game is amazing in almost every regard, as someone who has played almost every game in this legendary series. The world has a greater amount of depth than any previous Zelda game, it's almost impossible to do everything and the story is delightfully engaging. So yeah buy it.

I'll list my gripes with the game before continuing. Due to the open-ended nature of the game, some puzzles and aspects such as combat can feel almost challengless because any wacky or stupid solution you come up with will generally work; of course, this is also one of, if not the best aspect of the game but sometimes you might wish the puzzles were a bit "tighter". Also, and if you've played the game you know what I mean, they did NOT change the four main quests to account for how many of them the player has done (you can do them in any order) which leads to the cool yet almost identical cutscenes that play in every region's quest to become comically repetitive. Lastly there's too many blessing shrines that require no effort to get.

Okay now for good stuff :) 1. Ultrahand literally let's you do anything, in a game that would be perfectly fine without it
2. The temples are... Well half of them are excellent, 1 is awful and another is obviously the tutorial one so it gets a pass for its theming alone.
3. Sky islands are a joy to explore for the first time, some of my best memories in games were in them!
4. While it's frankly not too different to Breath of the Wild's, the world is such a joy to take in.
5. The largest new area I won't say much about is super fun to explore for me
6. And ultimately, it's a fantastic game that has minor flaws in certain segments yet nevertheless is an absolute must play best played at a slow and patient pace. PS: I haven't beaten the game yet I'm on the last of the temples

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
At first I thought this was gonna be just Botw with just new mechanics like the people in comments seem to mention( its too obvious they didnt play either games properly lmao) They revamped nearly each area topography, made over 80 side adventures which are chain side quests + over 180 side quests, they made 152 shrines with actually interesting stuff than botw, a whole underground area with full of hard monsters and a lot of loot. 380+ caves and nearly same amount of wells. They upped their game on dungeons and gave us 4 main dungeons + 1 optional dungeon in endgame. Increased enemy types so much and varied and they actually make us use all game mechanics connected to each other.

Some people will complain about the 1080p 30fps with dipping situation but lets face the fact that this game running on switch is like a miracle considering they made seamless transition between sky ground and depths + they made loading screens shorter. And the framedrop situation isn't because developers are lazy but they are stuck with an old console. So idk if that should actually affect the "game"s score when its not even games fault.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game is a great entry in the Zelda franchise and is absolutely worth a playthrough. I'd go so far as to say if you are going to play one game from the franchise in your life this is the one. That being said the game is full of issues that I think are indicative of Nintendo's lack of interest in pushing boundaries of any kind while also competing with its own characters lack of development and Zelda's own personal development being one of the coolest we have ever seen not just in this series but in many Video Game stories.

I like that they brought back the concept of the sages, having that portion of Zelda lore back in such a big game for the franchise was great. And seeing the first rulers of the land of Hyrule was equally mystifying and interesting as a long time fan of the series. But the sages themselves had zero character development. Even if we include what happened with them in the first game. e.g. Tulin the sage of Wind and a Rito is just a generic teenage kid. they do not appear to have any other defining traits aside from this. Riju is still *just* a Gerudo leader and Sidon is your run of the mill himbo. All of this culminates in their powers which are at best clunky to use, but most of the time they are just useless side mechanics that the game could easily have left out. While it is clear that the building was meant to be the star of this game one of, at least in this gamers opinions, best parts of Breath of the Wild was that the guardian abilities were supplemental to the runes that you collected at the beginning of the game. whether they were defensive or offensive, or hell just let you traverse the wind better, they all had a purpose and were easily used as you played the game unlike the sage powers in Tears of the Kingdom.

The boss fights were immaculate, and each one felt so unique. Finding them again in the depths and getting to play through them a second time with the slightly added difficulty of the gloom was a lot of fun. The Ganondorf fight while not initially at the epic scale I would have hoped for proved to be my favorite in the series. I felt like for the first time I had become strong enough to stand toe to toe with the demon king himself and the final form when it all took to the skies was breathtakingly epic.

Overall I did really enjoy this game, but unfortunately it just left me wanting in so many ways. Characters who didn't even begin to get a beefier backstory or even a whisper of growth throughout this ordeal were forced upon you, while the clunky mechanics and seeming lack of forethought made it strange to move through the world or even use the new abilities that were given to you. I see why this game is going to be the GOTY, but truly it does not deserve it and it's a shame that other titles that have more fleshed out stories and mechanics will be overlooked because this game lets you build a hover bike. I think the ending of this game is a perfect allegory to how I felt when I beat it. Like link sitting on the grass with nothing left to defeat in the world, all I wanted was a hug and instead I just saw some credits roll.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom es un juego muy esperado y ha recibido críticas muy positivas. Es una secuela directa de Breath of the Wild y se basa en lo que hizo Breath of the Wild anteriormente, refinando los sistemas del primer juego. El juego es tan amplio como profundo y algo que justifica cómodamente la espera de seis años. Es el juego de Zelda más narrativo1. El juego sigue siendo un caótico patio de recreo físico, pero es uno que es de alguna manera más amigable y en otros aspectos incluso más castigador que su predecesor.

IGN lo describe como una secuela notable que de alguna manera eleva aún más el listón hacia las nubes2. Este sandbox es más grande, más rico y de alguna manera aún más ambicioso, con nuevos sistemas creativos como la construcción de vehículos, la elaboración ridícula de armas y un mapa renovado de Hyrule con una cantidad vertiginosa de profundidad que profundiza aún más la exploración intoxicante que hizo que el original fuera tan cautivador. Breath of the Wild se sintió lejos de estar inacabado pero, inconcebiblemente, Tears of the Kingdom ha logrado hacerlo sentir como un primer borrador

En Metacritic, el juego tiene una puntuación Metascore de 96, lo que indica aclamación universal basada en 140 críticas. TheGamer lo llama una obra maestra que no solo iguala lo que vino antes, sino que hace todo lo posible para superarlo1.

En resumen, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom ha sido muy bien recibido por la crítica y parece ser una adición emocionante a la franquicia.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
After 150 hours, it's time to write a review. This game made me smile from the first day I played it to the day when I defeated Ganondorf, which was yesterday. At first, I thought it was nothing much different from BotW aside from the new abilities... but man I was I wrong.

But first, the cons. The story was a bit weak at first but gets better. I wish they changed how the armors looked even a little bit because most of them are exactly what they looked like in BotW. I was also hoping for more variations with the korok challenges. It is the same Hyrule from BotW... but tbf, the sky islands, depths, caves and wells added a lot more places to explore and discover. And with the overworld monsters, I was expecting more of a challenge.

The more hours I spent, the more different gameplay opportunities open up. Fiddling with zonai devices and fuse is funny as it is rewarding. Ascend is a god-sent ability that is very satisfying to use. The puzzles, places, bosses, and even the HUD is curated for a unique gaming experience which is what I personally think Zelda games do best. Not to mention there are several ways to solve a singular problem. I am a trial and error type of guy so it resonated with me very well.

I mentioned that the story is a bit weak in the beginning but it got better and better especially in the final sequences of the main quest. I recommend getting the tears in order as it will provide you a more coherent story-telling experience!

I love this game to the point that after 150 hours I wish there was more content even though I've only completed about 2/3 of the sidequests and about 90% of the shrines. I'll certainly keep playing and wait for the DLC (no official announcement yet but I hope there is a DLC). If that DLC didn't come after I 100% the game quests and shrines, I am considering another playthrough.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
What. A. Game.

They took one of the best games ever made, 5-6 years of development time, and a big team of passionate video game developers... How could this ever go wrong? They could have made a record breaking game with just 2-3 years but no, they decided they want to take their time with it, and they did it again. They made it even better somehow, no idea how, but they did.

The story is so amazing and definitely deserves a spot as one of the most beautiful stories in the Zelda franchise. We also got a lot of lore and learned more about the Zonai, which I really enjoyed. I really hope the next game builds even more on this, all these time lines and essays about when each game takes place can give one a real headache.

The enemies in this game are crazy. I do still miss the guardians from BOTW, but the new ones more than fill their spot. I love how you are just exploring the world, picking up some mushrooms, looking at some deer, and then all of the sudden the sky turns red, five hands come out of the ground, and they just start coming after you. They pick you up, start infecting you with gloom, you try to run away but they are too fast and catch you again... So scary and I love it. The same with the 3 headed dragon, I just wanted to take a picture of it and then it chased me for what felt like half of the map and then just laser beamed me. It feels amazing progressing through the game and then being strong enough to fight monsters that felt unbeatable, to killing them with ease.

And they added one of the best mechanics, fuse. It's honestly so funny people complaining that it's just Minecraft, like what? Have you ever played Minecraft in your life? When do you put a fan on a stick and fly on a hoverboard in Minecraft? When do you find a fossil in a cave, put a float ball beneath it, put canons on it, and have a skeleton pirate ship in Minecraft? And even IF it were similar to Minecraft, which as someone who has played Minecraft for years can confirm it's not, how would that be a bad thing? Minecraft is one of the most loved games, even in 2023 and it's over a decade old. No idea what people are smoking nowadays, but I built myself an awesome robot snail that freezes all enemies in an area and I love it. I call him Garry.

It's too much stuff for one review, you could write a whole book on this game, you could easily make a 10 hour youtube video just talking about this masterpiece. It's the middle of the year as of writing this review, and there is not a single doubt in my mind that this is GOTY23. Games like this don't come around often, so take your time with it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: I generally loved this game. There is one thing both BOTW and TOTK are lacking, and it’s the fact that after you complete the main quest, you can’t  continue to engage with the game in a way that flows naturally. It’s unsatisfying that you can’t continue to complete the rest of the quests while characters recognize you defeated Ganon once more. Maybe you find Zelda in different areas of the map, walks around with you helping to complete missions, adds commentary, whatever. I hope they could restructure the game in this way in the future - I would love to see a third game or at least a DLC for TOTK.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
Remember when you explored the Great Plateau, thinking "this game has so much potential"? Well, after a couple of hours Tears of the Kingdom absolutely DESTROYS its predecessor with new crazy abilites, a new level design even better than in the past, a refined sound system, the greatest opening to a videogame I've ever seen, infinite creative possibilities, a much improved immersiveness with the environment and npcs, and much more. Wow.
Yes, there are many technical problems. They are much more present than in Breath of the Wild, but they rarely ruin the experience and the feeling is always that they are worth resisting with the amazing game you are playing.
This is without any sort of doubt the best game I've ever played and you should play it

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
!!!SPOILERS FOR MAIN STORY!!!


Just the fact that you get put into gameplay at the start of the game so you can adapt to the controls is Awsome, and the discovery of the dried up Ganondorf (I’ll say Ganon for short but I KNOW THE DIFFERENCE) which then wakes up and somehow knows the name of Zelda and Link is so cryptic the first time you get to it, but becomes clear when the game ends. Also Zelda becoming a Dragon and staying one for 1000+ years just to heal up the Master Sword for Link to defeat the Demon King is totally unexpected. The 4 new powers are all useful and almost never situational (I like Recall and Ascend the most) and they let you do all sorts of stuff like having infinite battery on cars [I won’t say how >:)], or visit places you never even dreamed of in BOTW. The sky islands are great to explore, and the depths, while being really dark and scary when you first enter them are somewhat easy to explore since the lightroots are very visible so you have an objective every time you visit it.
10/10 game, would never say anything bad about it.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: This game is REALLY fun. Even if you've played Breath of the Wild, there's mountains of new content in the sky, surface, and underworld that it exceeds Breath of the Wild both in terms of quality and quantity. Ultrahand is genuinely one of my favorite game mechanics to ever be implemented into any game. Ever. The puzzles you can solve and the contraptions you can create with it are beyond fun, and while a few puzzles are admittedly tedious, the amount of other amazing puzzles overshadows the bad. The boss fights are a lot more fun and interesting, the combat is good and really satisfying, and even if you start playing and the whole game just doesn't feel right, like how I went into the game, just know that it gets way, way, WAY better, and you will NOT be disappointed. All you need is to see all the surprises the game holds. It is ABSOLUTELY worth 70 dollars and don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

Review: Estamos ante una obra maestra. Llevo unas 18 horas jugadas y estoy literalmente al principio del videojuego, pero es que esas 18 horas se sienten como media hora de cualquier otro juego que en 18 horas lo terminas. Es una pasada la variedad de enemigos la enormisimidad de los mapas que tiene. Porque si piensas que la novedad son las islas flotantes, espera y verás... Estan ocurriendo cosas a cada rincón que mires. Es literalmente imposible aburrirse. Tiene una gran variedad de enemigos, muchísimos más que el Breath of the wild. El doblaje al castellano es buenísimo, solo siento que no haya más escenas con audio pero bueno los juegos japoneses son así, más de texto leído. En cuanto al frame rate. Es cierto que no es perfecto pero la Nintendo Switch no da para más y  no son nada grave tampoco estas caídas, ocurren cuando hay muchos enemigos y además haces volar todo por los aires, o sea necesitas muchísima carga en el juego para desestabilizar la tasa de cuadros, pero no es culpa del videojuego que está optimizadísimo, si no de la consola y no se puede ni debe penalizar al juego por el hardware donde se ejecuta. El juego se merece los 10 de la prensa y los 10 de los usuarios. Creo que esta vez el GOTY ya ha salido, queda mucho año y veremos, pero lo tienen difícil los demás.

In addition, there are many completely new areas like the sky islands and the depths that you can explore for tens of hours alone. I also enjoy the new abilities since they can interact with the world even more than BOTWs abilities could and give you even more space for creativity. Most of my expectations for this game have been outdone by the zelda team. Out of 100 I would give this game 95-97 since my main grudge with it and its prequel, the weapon breaking system, hasnt been addressed the way i was hoping for. Still i can see this being one of the games people are going to remember fondly for many years.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review: Many have their criticisms with this game on the basis that it reuses assets and feels like botw DLC. I completely disagree. Firstly, a game should be rated by how fun your experience with it was. It really shouldn't matter that some aspects of the previous game stay. In fact, since botw was such a great game, it might be for the best that we get the same major elements in a vastly newer light. And this game is indeed REALLY fun. Not one moment do you feel like you have to go searching for something new to do, like what sometimes happens in the botw late game. Just following the main story opens up infinite branches of adventures, and each branch leads to new adventures just as exciting. The map, while technically the same, is changed to such a degree that exploring it feels brand new again. That's not to mention the entire depth map (as detailed and as large as Hyrule), which is plenty to satisfy that need to discover a completely new world. If I had to say something negative of this game, it would be that the skies could be expanded further, especially considering how heavily it was featured in the marketing. However, if the only core complaint of this game is that there isn't enough of it, I think that only goes to show how amazing it is.

Title: the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom
Review:
This game is a bittersweet masterpiece, since while it is truly amazing and certainly a lot of fun, just thinking about how much more mind-blowing this game would have been as the first introduction to the BotW formula makes me feel regretful we didn't see all of these features and ideas in the original. This truly is a sequel which expands upon, improves, and doubles down on every design choice and feature of the original. Breath of the Wild was an incredible game but it mainly succeeded because of its exploration and brilliantly constructed open world. While it had fun combat and puzzle design, and a nice minimalist story which leaned on subtlety and environmental storytelling, these were not the strongest points of the game - they simply were good, while the world and exploration was great. 
Tears of the Kingdom feels like it knew this about its predecessor and revitalised and improved upon every aspect of the original. The combat is better, and there is more variety in moves, abilities, and enemy variety. The movement and traversal options have been expanded to a ludicrous degree. The puzzles and abilities are both vastly superior to the original. The dungeons are more inventive and unique from one another. The story is more elaborate and characters are more memorable. And the final boss is vastly superior to the original. Everything that was good in the first game is better in the second.
The only thing which has not changed as much is the world. Hyrule has had many subtle changes all across its landscape, and structures and settlements have changed dramatically. But it is still functionally the same world from the original. If you have played the oroginal as much as I have, then you know that there simply isnt as much to explore and discover in Hyrule this time around.
The first game had an atmosphere of discovery - sinking into a vast and ruined kingdom to uncover all sorts of fascinating experiences and characters and places. This was the beating heart of the game and the wanderlust of players is what drove them to explore the map.
This game has an atmosphere of rediscovery instead. Rather than exploring a world for the first time, you are revisiting a world that is very familiar to you and finding out everything which has changed over the years. The core of this exploration is more focused on tracking down leads and rumours about what crazy events have taken place all across the world, and investigating them at your own leisure. I do not mean to say that this style of exploration is bad in some way - I was enthralled by it for dozens of hours, writing down all the rumours I had heard from NPCs and all the interesting things I had seen in the distance that I wanted to uncover later. I tracked down all these leads and gradually made so many amazing discoveries. This sort of exploration is incredibly enjoyable and rewarding. BUT - I do prefer BotW's style. While there are some new areas that bring back that BotW feeling, namely exploring the sky islands and the depths, the islands are too few in number to really scratch that itch (I loved all of them, but they don't constitute a brand new map), and the depths lacked the same visual and functional variety as the different provinces in the overworld, making them less enjoyable to explore. It is in this way that I think, having played BotW so much, TotK just does not capture the same essence, rather it goes in a slightly different direction; one I enjoyed, but ultimately not as much as the first. 
But this game is also a bittersweet masterpiece for this exact reason. BotW was already a 10/10, but I cannot imagine how blown away I would have been if I had skipped it and played TotK blind. The entire world of Hyrule AND the Depths AND the Sky islands? I would lose my mind. No game would ever come close, and even if the world isn't as novel after BotW, the variety in this exploration and rediscovery makes the game's pacing so engaging and addictive. You can ride around the overworld for hours, then find a chasm and dive into the Depths, fighting minibosses and enemy camps until you're too burnt out, then ascend to the overworld and take a trip on a dragon to the Sky Islands, soaring around, solving puzzles, collecting fairies and treasure maps, so you can dive back to the depths to find where they lead, and go back to the overworld to ride to the next region. The game has a phenomenal loop of all sorts of incredible experiences.
I am upset a little that this game didn't have a brand new overworld like BotW, but I am by no means disappointed in this game. This game is a victory for Nintendo for proving that you can make a sequel to a boundary-breaking masterpiece without milking all the tried and true mechanics dry. This game surpasses the original in every way, while offering a different sort of exploration that is still equally enjoyable and satisfying. 
It is just in this last detail, that I slightly prefer BotW.
